resources.name: MAST (Mikulski Archive for Space Telescopes)
resources.summary: STScI archive holding JWST, HST, TESS, Kepler/K2, GALEX and Pan-STARRS data; all observations become public after any proprietary period (typically 12 months for JWST/HST GO programs) and public holdings are mirrored to AWS.
resources.access: Web portal at mast.stsci.edu, or `pip install astroquery` then `from astroquery.mast import Observations`; cloud reads via `Observations.enable_cloud_dataset()` against s3://stpubdata (anonymous, no AWS account needed).
resources.notes: A free MyST account is only needed to download proprietary-period data you are authorized for; everything public is anonymous-access.

resources.name: ESA Gaia Archive
resources.summary: Gaia DR3 (2022) gives positions, parallaxes, proper motions and photometry for ~1.8 billion sources; DR4, covering 5.5 years of data at ~400 TB including epoch-level data, is scheduled for 2 December 2026.
resources.access: ADQL queries in the web archive, or `pip install astroquery` then `from astroquery.gaia import Gaia; Gaia.launch_job('SELECT ...')`; bulk files via direct download. Subsets also served by CDS, AIP and other partner centres.
resources.notes: Anonymous queries have row/job limits; a free account lifts them and keeps query history. ESA has announced breaking interface changes to the archive in preparation for DR4's much larger volume.

resources.name: SDSS SkyServer
resources.summary: SQL interface to all Sloan Digital Sky Survey releases; DR20 (30 July 2026, third SDSS-V release) adds over 3 million optical spectra from the Black Hole Mapper and Milky Way Mapper programs.
resources.access: Free-form SQL in the browser at skyserver.sdss.org; longer jobs via CasJobs (free account); `astroquery.sdss` for scripted access; flat files from data.sdss.org.
resources.notes: CasJobs and SciServer compute require a free email registration; SkyServer quick queries have row/time limits.

resources.name: DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys
resources.summary: Deep grz imaging and source catalogues from DECam, BASS and MzLS built for DESI targeting; the sky viewer serves image cutouts of any position on demand.
resources.access: Cutout API, e.g. https://www.legacysurvey.org/viewer/cutout.fits?ra=180.0&dec=30.0&layer=ls-dr10&pixscale=0.262 (also cutout.jpg); interactive viewer at legacysurvey.org/viewer; catalogues queryable via NOIRLab Astro Data Lab TAP.
resources.notes: Cutout service is rate-limited for bulk use; for large jobs download bricks directly or query Data Lab.

resources.name: DESI Data Archive
resources.summary: Public data from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument; DR1 (March 2025) contains spectra and redshifts for ~18.7 million galaxies, quasars and stars.
resources.access: Direct HTTPS download at data.desi.lbl.gov; individual spectra retrievable without bulk download via the SPARCL service (`pip install sparclclient`) at NOIRLab.
resources.notes: Full-release files are very large; SPARCL or Astro Data Lab queries are the practical route on a laptop.

resources.name: ZTF (Zwicky Transient Facility) public data
resources.summary: Northern-sky time-domain survey; bimonthly public data releases of images and light curves are served at IRSA, and the real-time alert stream is redistributed publicly.
resources.access: IRSA web tools and light-curve API; `astroquery.ipac.irsa` for scripted queries; alerts via community brokers (ALeRCE, Fink, Lasair, ANTARES) or bulk alert archive at ztf.uw.edu.
resources.notes: Partnership-time data are proprietary; the public surveys are fully open. Light-curve queries scale poorly for millions of objects - use the bulk release files for statistics work.

resources.name: ALeRCE alert broker
resources.summary: Astronomical alert broker ingesting the ZTF stream and Rubin/LSST alerts (one of the official Rubin brokers), with machine-learning classifications, light curves and cross-matches for millions of transients and variables.
resources.access: Web explorer at alerce.online; Python client `pip install alerce` then `from alerce.core import Alerce`; public HTTP API.
resources.notes: Alternatives with similar free access include Fink (fink-broker.org), Lasair and ANTARES; all serve the world-public Rubin alert stream, so no data rights are needed for alerts.

resources.name: ASAS-SN Sky Patrol
resources.summary: All-Sky Automated Survey for Supernovae; Sky Patrol V2.0 serves continuously updated V- and g-band light curves for 111 million catalogued targets, with photometry typically available within about an hour of observation.
resources.access: Web query at asas-sn.osu.edu (arbitrary-position photometry) and the V2.0 interface at asas-sn.ifa.hawaii.edu/skypatrol/ with a Python client (pyasassn; docs at asas-sn.ifa.hawaii.edu/documentation).
resources.notes: Shallow depth (small telephoto lenses) - roughly 17-18 mag limit; ideal for bright variables, supernovae and long baselines rather than faint sources.

resources.name: AAVSO (American Association of Variable Star Observers)
resources.summary: The AAVSO International Database holds over a century of variable-star photometry contributed by amateurs and professionals; the companion VSX index catalogues over 2 million known variable stars.
resources.access: Light Curve Generator and data download on aavso.org; VSX search at vsx.aavso.org (also mirrored in VizieR); submit your own observations via WebObs after obtaining a free observer code.
resources.notes: Membership is paid but is NOT required to access data, submit observations, or propose new variables to VSX; registration (free) is required for submissions.

resources.name: GWOSC (Gravitational Wave Open Science Center)
resources.summary: Public LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA strain data and event catalogues (through GWTC-4, released 2025, covering O4a), plus tutorials and the annual Open Data Workshop materials.
resources.access: Event portal and bulk downloads at gwosc.org; `pip install gwpy` then `TimeSeries.fetch_open_data('H1', t0, t1)`; the `gwosc` and `pycbc` packages for catalog queries and analysis.
resources.notes: Strain data are released after a proprietary period, so the most recent observing-run segments lag public availability.

resources.name: CHIME/FRB Catalogs
resources.summary: CHIME/FRB Catalog 2 (2026) contains 4,539 fast radio bursts from 3,641 unique sources detected between July 2018 and September 2023, an 8.5-fold increase over Catalog 1 (536 FRBs, 2021).
resources.access: Browse and download via the catalog site; machine-readable data and utilities via the open-data portal chime-frb-open-data.github.io and `pip install cfod`.
resources.notes: Raw voltage/intensity data are not fully public; the catalogs contain burst properties and selected waterfall data.

resources.name: Breakthrough Listen Open Data Archive
resources.summary: Multi-petabyte public archive of radio (and some optical) SETI observations from the Green Bank Telescope, Parkes and the Automated Planet Finder, the largest open SETI dataset in existence.
resources.access: Search and direct download at breakthroughinitiatives.org/opendatasearch (beta interface at seti.berkeley.edu/opendata); read files with `pip install blimpy`; Doppler-drift searches with `turbo_seti`.
resources.notes: Individual filterbank/HDF5 files are often several GB and formats require specialized tools; start with the tutorial datasets rather than raw voltages.

resources.name: Fermi Science Support Center
resources.summary: All Fermi-LAT photon data have been public immediately since August 2009, with continuous all-sky coverage; GBM burst data and the 4FGL source catalogs are also served.
resources.access: LAT data server web query at fermi.gsfc.nasa.gov/ssc/; analysis with fermitools (conda install from the fermi channel) and `pip install fermipy`.
resources.notes: No registration for data, but LAT likelihood analysis has a steep learning curve and needs several GB of spacecraft/diffuse files.

resources.name: IceCube public data releases
resources.summary: Public neutrino datasets including IceTracks-DR2 (released May 2026): 14 years of track-like neutrino candidates from April 2008 to May 2022 for point-source searches, with documentation and example analyses.
resources.access: Direct download from the data-releases page (files hosted on Harvard Dataverse); CSV/HDF5 formats readable with pandas.
resources.notes: These are curated event lists and instrument response functions, not raw detector data; questions go to analysis@icecube.wisc.edu.

resources.name: NASA Exoplanet Archive
resources.summary: Vetted database of confirmed exoplanets and their measured parameters, with linked literature references; listed 6,128 confirmed planets as of February 2026 (the 6,000 milestone was passed in September 2025).
resources.access: Interactive tables in the browser; TAP/API queries; `pip install astroquery` then `from astroquery.ipac.nexsci.nasa_exoplanet_archive import NasaExoplanetArchive`.
resources.notes: The companion ExoFOP service (exofop.ipac.caltech.edu) coordinates follow-up of TESS and K2 candidates; browsing is open and contributing observations needs only a free account - a genuine route for amateurs with modest telescopes.

resources.name: Minor Planet Center
resources.summary: The IAU's official clearinghouse for astrometric observations and orbits of over 1.4 million minor planets and comets; publishes orbit files (MPCORB), observation databases and NEO confirmation lists.
resources.access: Web services and database queries at minorplanetcenter.net; bulk MPCORB downloads; astrometry submissions accepted from anyone observing from a site with an MPC observatory code.
resources.notes: Submitting observations requires obtaining an observatory code (free, demonstrated astrometric accuracy required) - a long-standing amateur-professional pathway, now also the public route for Rubin solar-system discoveries.

resources.name: JPL Solar System Dynamics (Horizons & SBDB)
resources.summary: Horizons computes high-precision ephemerides for essentially every known solar-system body plus spacecraft; the Small-Body Database serves orbital and physical parameters with close-approach data.
resources.access: Web app at ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/horizons/; REST APIs at ssd-api.jpl.nasa.gov (no key needed); scripted access via `astroquery.jplhorizons` and `astroquery.jplsbdb`.

resources.name: VizieR
resources.summary: CDS library of more than 20,000 published astronomical catalogues and tables, from small journal tables to full surveys, all queryable through uniform Virtual Observatory interfaces.
resources.access: Web queries at vizier.cds.unistra.fr; `pip install astroquery` then `from astroquery.vizier import Vizier`; TAP endpoint for ADQL (tapvizier.cds.unistra.fr).
resources.notes: Default query row limits are low (50); set Vizier.ROW_LIMIT = -1 in astroquery to retrieve full tables.

resources.name: SIMBAD
resources.summary: CDS reference database resolving names, cross-identifications, basic measurements and complete literature links for over 10 million astronomical objects outside the solar system.
resources.access: Web queries at simbad.cds.unistra.fr; `from astroquery.simbad import Simbad`; TAP service for bulk cross-identification.
resources.notes: Part of the wider free CDS ecosystem: the Aladin interactive sky atlas (aladin.cds.unistra.fr, desktop and Lite web version) and the CDS X-Match service for crossmatching billion-row catalogues.

resources.name: NED (NASA/IPAC Extragalactic Database)
resources.summary: Cross-matched multiwavelength positions, redshifts, photometry, images and literature for hundreds of millions of extragalactic objects, fused from major sky surveys and journal tables.
resources.access: Web interface at ned.ipac.caltech.edu; `from astroquery.ipac.ned import Ned`; TAP and object-lookup APIs.
resources.notes: Complements SIMBAD: NED is deeper for galaxies and redshift bookkeeping; SIMBAD is stronger for Galactic objects.

resources.name: ESO Science Archive
resources.summary: Raw and pipeline-processed data from the VLT/VLTI, VISTA, VST, La Silla telescopes and APEX; observations become public after the proprietary period (typically one year), and processed science-ready collections are served alongside raw frames.
resources.access: Science portal at archive.eso.org/scienceportal; programmatic access via `astroquery.eso` and TAP; direct download of processed data products.
resources.notes: Some services (large raw-data requests, calSelector) work best with a free ESO User Portal account.

resources.name: ALMA Science Archive
resources.summary: All ALMA observations become public after a one-year proprietary period; the archive serves raw visibilities and, increasingly, imaged data products for thousands of projects.
resources.access: Query interface at almascience.org/aq (no login to search or download public data); `astroquery.alma` for scripted download.
resources.notes: Reprocessing raw visibilities requires CASA plus substantial disk and CPU; look for archival imaged products (continuum/line cubes) first, or use the ARI-L/ALMINER value-added products.

resources.name: HEASARC
resources.summary: NASA's archive for X-ray and gamma-ray astronomy: Chandra, XMM-Newton, Swift, NuSTAR, NICER, IXPE, Fermi and dozens of historical missions, plus the LAMBDA CMB data holdings.
resources.access: Xamin/Browse query tools at heasarc.gsfc.nasa.gov; `astroquery.heasarc`; analysis with the free HEASoft suite (XSPEC etc.); Chandra-specific tools via the CXC (cxc.cfa.harvard.edu, CIAO software).
resources.notes: Data are free with no gates, but high-energy analysis (response files, effective areas) has real overhead; Swift and NICER are the gentlest entry points.

resources.name: Helioviewer
resources.summary: Browse, animate and export solar imagery from SDO, SOHO, STEREO and other missions, spanning decades of observations, in a zoomable web interface backed by a public API.
resources.access: Web app at helioviewer.org; REST API at api.helioviewer.org; Python wrapper `pip install hvpy`.
resources.notes: Serves browse-quality JPEG2000 images; for science-grade SDO FITS files use the JSOC export system (jsoc.stanford.edu) or SunPy's Fido search, both free.

resources.name: SDOML (SDO Machine Learning Dataset)
resources.summary: Curated, calibration-corrected SDO dataset for machine learning: AIA images 2010-2020 in 10 wavebands at 512x512 and 6-minute cadence, HMI vector magnetograms at 12-minute cadence, and EVE irradiance 2010-2014, all in cloud-friendly Zarr format.
resources.access: Read directly from AWS S3 with zarr/fsspec (bucket listed at registry.opendata.aws/sdoml-fdl); loaders and examples at sdoml.github.io and github.com/SDOML.
resources.notes: Downscaled from full 4096x4096 resolution by design; for full-resolution science data go to JSOC instead.

resources.name: e-CALLISTO
resources.summary: Worldwide network of low-cost CALLISTO radio spectrometers monitoring solar radio bursts around the clock; daily FITS spectrograms from all stations are collected centrally and archived publicly.
resources.access: Browse and download gzipped FITS files at e-callisto.org/Data/data.html; daily quicklook plots and automatic burst lists on the same site.
resources.notes: Data quality varies by station (radio-frequency interference); the network also welcomes new hosts - the spectrometer hardware is intentionally low-cost, making this a practical instrument route for individuals and small institutions.

resources.name: SPHEREx Archive at IRSA
resources.summary: NASA's SPHEREx (launched March 2025) is performing the first all-sky 0.75-5 micron spectral survey in 102 bands; IRSA publishes new Quick Release spectral images weekly (QR2, with improved calibration, since October 2025), with data also mirrored to AWS.
resources.access: IRSA search tools, TAP/ADQL queries and the SPHEREx Source Discovery and Mosaic tools; cloud access via the public AWS bucket (registry.opendata.aws/spherex-qr); documentation at caltech-ipac.github.io/spherex-archive-documentation.
resources.notes: QR2 supersedes QR1; higher-level products (full-sky maps, catalogues) roll out over the mission's remaining years.

resources.name: Euclid Q1 Data Release
resources.summary: Euclid Quick Release 1 (19 March 2025): ~30 TB of VIS/NISP imaging, slitless spectra and catalogues over ~63 deg2 of the Euclid Deep Fields North, Fornax and South plus LDN1641.
resources.access: ESA Euclid Science Archive (linked from the Q1 data page); full mirror at IRSA with TAP/ADQL catalog queries and AWS cloud copies; tutorial notebooks at caltech-ipac.github.io/irsa-tutorials.
resources.notes: Q1 is single-visit depth over deep fields only; substantially larger cosmology-scale releases are planned as the survey progresses.

resources.name: Rubin Observatory / LSST data
resources.summary: Data Preview 1 (2025) covers seven ~1 deg2 commissioning fields; Early Data Preview 2 (2026) adds LSSTCam observations from April 2025 to January 2026; the real-time alert stream (design rate ~10 million alerts/night) has been flowing to brokers since February 2026.
resources.access: Rubin Science Platform (data.lsst.cloud) notebooks and TAP for data-rights holders; alerts are world-public through brokers (ALeRCE, Fink, Lasair, ANTARES and others) with no data rights needed; solar-system detections flow to the Minor Planet Center.
resources.notes: RSP accounts and pixel/catalogue releases are restricted to data-rights holders (US- and Chile-affiliated researchers plus named international in-kind contributors) until releases become world-public after a delay; unaffiliated researchers can still do real science today via the public alert stream and MPC.

resources.name: NASA Planetary Data System (PDS)
resources.summary: Permanent archive of data from NASA planetary missions (Mars orbiters and rovers, Cassini, New Horizons, Juno, OSIRIS-REx and more), organized in discipline nodes with peer-reviewed data standards.
resources.access: Search at pds.nasa.gov; direct HTTP download from discipline-node servers; image-focused browsing via the Cartography and Imaging Sciences node (PDS Imaging Atlas).
resources.notes: Navigation across nodes takes practice; the SPICE toolkit (NAIF, naif.jpl.nasa.gov; Python wrapper `pip install spiceypy`) is the free standard for the geometry files that accompany most datasets.

resources.name: Transient Name Server (TNS)
resources.summary: The IAU's official registry for reporting and naming astronomical transients; essentially all supernova discoveries and classifications flow through it, searchable by anyone.
resources.access: Public web search without login; reporting discoveries or classifications requires a free registered account (individual or group); rate-limited REST API with an API key for bots.
resources.notes: A working route for amateurs who discover transients: register, report with required astrometry/photometry, and the object receives an official designation.

resources.name: Astropy
resources.summary: The core Python package for astronomy: coordinates, WCS, FITS and table I/O, units, time systems and cosmology; foundation of virtually the entire Python astronomy ecosystem of affiliated packages.
resources.access: `pip install astropy` (or conda); documentation at docs.astropy.org.
resources.notes: BSD-licensed, community-developed; affiliated packages (photutils, specutils, regions, ccdproc) cover most reduction tasks.

resources.name: astroquery
resources.summary: One Python package with uniform interfaces to dozens of archives and services - MAST, Gaia, SIMBAD, VizieR, IRSA, NED, ESO, ALMA, JPL Horizons, HEASARC and more - so a laptop can script against most of the world's astronomy data.
resources.access: `pip install astroquery`; e.g. `from astroquery.simbad import Simbad; Simbad.query_object('M31')`.
resources.notes: Individual services keep their own rate limits and occasional required credentials; module namespaces changed in recent versions (e.g. astroquery.ipac.ned), so match examples to your installed version.

resources.name: Lightkurve
resources.summary: Python package for Kepler, K2 and TESS photometry: one-line search and download from MAST, detrending, periodograms and transit searches with well-documented tutorials.
resources.access: `pip install lightkurve`; e.g. `import lightkurve as lk; lk.search_lightcurve('Pi Mensae', mission='TESS').download().plot()`.
resources.notes: Runs comfortably on a laptop for single targets; for bulk work use the TIKE cloud platform where the same data live next to the compute.

resources.name: SunPy
resources.summary: Core Python library for solar data analysis: the Fido interface searches and downloads from VSO, JSOC and other archives, with Map and TimeSeries classes for images and light curves.
resources.access: `pip install sunpy`; e.g. `from sunpy.net import Fido, attrs as a; Fido.search(a.Time(...), a.Instrument.aia)`.
resources.notes: JSOC bulk exports ask for a (free) registered email address.

resources.name: Stellarium
resources.summary: Open-source desktop planetarium rendering a realistic sky with large star catalogues, telescope control, and observation planning; also available as Stellarium Web in the browser.
resources.access: Direct download (Windows/macOS/Linux, GPL) from stellarium.org; browser version at stellarium-web.org.
resources.notes: Mobile apps are paid; desktop and web versions are fully free.

resources.name: Skyfield
resources.summary: Pure-Python astronomy engine computing positions of planets, comets, asteroids and Earth satellites directly from JPL ephemerides and MPC/Celestrak data, with results consistent with Horizons.
resources.access: `pip install skyfield`; e.g. load('de421.bsp') then observe planets from any topocentric location.
resources.notes: Downloads ephemeris files on first use (tens of MB); ideal for observation planning, satellite passes and occultation work without any web service dependency.

resources.name: REBOUND
resources.summary: Open-source N-body integrator (IAS15, WHFast and other symplectic schemes) used across planetary dynamics and planetesimal studies; runs real research problems on a laptop.
resources.access: `pip install rebound`; add `reboundx` for extra forces (GR, radiation pressure, migration).

resources.name: TOPCAT
resources.summary: Desktop Java tool for interactive work on large tables: million-row crossmatching, sky and 3D plotting, and built-in Virtual Observatory access (TAP, cone search) to services like VizieR and Gaia; actively maintained (v4.10-6, May 2026).
resources.access: Download the topcat jar from the website and run `java -jar topcat-full.jar`; command-line sibling STILTS for scripted pipelines.
resources.notes: Handles tables of millions of rows on modest hardware; the standard answer to 'how do I crossmatch two catalogues without writing code'.

resources.name: SciX / NASA ADS
resources.summary: The field's free bibliographic database: complete refereed astrophysics literature plus preprints and gray literature, over 30 million records with citation graphs; ADS (ui.adsabs.harvard.edu) is transitioning to the SciX interface during 2026.
resources.access: Search free at scixplorer.org (no account needed); private libraries and saved searches with a free account; free API token for scripted queries (e.g. `pip install ads`).
resources.notes: Indexes and links to full text but does not itself unlock paywalled journal PDFs; arXiv links cover most of the field in practice.

resources.name: arXiv astro-ph
resources.summary: The astrophysics preprint server, running since 1992; near-universal practice in the field means the freely readable preprint version exists for the large majority of current astronomy papers.
resources.access: Read free at arxiv.org (six astro-ph subcategories); daily listings and RSS; submission is free with an arXiv account.
resources.notes: First-time submitters without an institutional email may need an endorsement from an established arXiv author - a real but usually surmountable hurdle for independent researchers.

resources.name: The Open Journal of Astrophysics
resources.summary: Peer-reviewed arXiv-overlay journal covering astrophysics and cosmology: submission, refereeing and publication are all free of charge, funded by Maynooth Academic Publishing.
resources.access: Post your paper to arXiv, then submit the arXiv ID through astro.theoj.org for peer review.
resources.notes: No APC and no reader paywall; indexed and citable. A realistic venue for researchers without APC funds.

resources.name: Research Notes of the AAS (RNAAS)
resources.summary: Venue for brief communications (max 1,500 words, one figure or table): free to read, currently no author charge, each note gets a DOI and ADS indexing and is typically published within ~72 hours of receipt.
resources.access: Submit via the AAS journals submission system (AAS membership not required); LaTeX/Word templates provided.
resources.notes: Not peer reviewed (editor-checked only) and not copy-edited - suitable for negative results, follow-up observations, code/data announcements; a practical first publication route for individuals and amateurs.

resources.name: Astronomy & Astrophysics (A&A)
resources.summary: Major astronomy journal, fully open access since 2022 under the Subscribe-to-Open model - 2026 is the fifth consecutive year with no article processing charges for authors and free reading for everyone.
resources.access: Standard manuscript submission at aanda.org; no APC invoice under S2O.
resources.notes: S2O is renewed annually and depends on library subscriptions; A&A has said recent thresholds were met only narrowly, so the no-APC status should be re-checked each year. Page limits and language-editing policies apply.

resources.name: JOSS (Journal of Open Source Software)
resources.summary: Free, developer-friendly peer-reviewed journal for research software; astronomy packages routinely publish here to make their code citable, with open review conducted on GitHub.
resources.access: Submit a repository with a short paper.md via joss.theoj.org; review happens in a public GitHub issue; no charges.
resources.notes: The software itself must be open-source with a substantial scholarly effort; small scripts are rejected as out of scope.

resources.name: IAU Office of Astronomy for Development grants
resources.summary: Annual open call funding astronomy-for-development projects worldwide; the 2026 call earmarked EUR 60,000 total, with past project grants of EUR 1,000-15,000 (average around EUR 5,000).
resources.access: Two-stage online application (concept then full proposal) via astro4dev.org/cfp; open to anyone from anywhere in the world.
resources.notes: Funds development/education/community impact projects that use astronomy, not pure research programs; the 2026 deadline (31 May) has passed - watch for the next annual call.

resources.name: Planetary Society Shoemaker NEO Grants
resources.summary: Grants (typically $5,000-12,000) for advanced amateur and under-funded professional astronomers anywhere in the world to find, track and characterize near-Earth objects; the 2025 round awarded $87,562 to ten observers in eight countries.
resources.access: Apply during announced rounds via the program page (proposal describing your observing program and equipment upgrade).
resources.notes: One of very few funding lines explicitly open to unaffiliated observers. The Planetary Society's separate STEP Grants fund larger open-call science/technology projects in planetary exploration, planetary defense and the search for life.

resources.name: AAS Chrétien International Research Grants
resources.summary: Up to $20,000 available each year from the American Astronomical Society to support international collaborative projects in observational astronomy, emphasizing long-term visits between countries.
resources.access: Application through the AAS grants page during the annual cycle.
resources.notes: Open to astronomers worldwide but requires a PhD or equivalent; graduate students are not eligible.

resources.name: OpenStax Astronomy 2e
resources.summary: Full peer-reviewed introductory astronomy textbook (Fraknoi, Morrison & Wolff), free to read online or download as PDF under a CC BY license; the standard free text for a first course.
resources.access: Read in browser or direct PDF download at openstax.org; no account needed.
resources.notes: Introductory level - a bridge into the field, not a graduate reference.

resources.name: Essential Radio Astronomy
resources.summary: Condon & Ransom's graduate radio astronomy textbook (Princeton, 2016), whose full course version is freely readable online by agreement with the publisher; the canonical text NRAO itself teaches from.
resources.access: Read free at the NRAO course site (science.nrao.edu/opportunities/courses/era); print edition sold by Princeton University Press.

resources.name: Learn Astropy
resources.summary: The Astropy Project's curated tutorials and guides - executable Jupyter notebooks covering FITS handling, coordinates, photometry, spectroscopy and archive queries, maintained by the package developers themselves.
resources.access: Browse and download notebooks at learn.astropy.org; run locally or on any free notebook service.

resources.name: Dynamics and Astrophysics of Galaxies (galaxiesbook.org)
resources.summary: Jo Bovy's graduate textbook on galactic dynamics and astrophysics, published in print by Princeton (2026) with the complete interactive web version free, including runnable in-browser Python examples and animations.
resources.access: Read free at galaxiesbook.org; code examples run in the browser.
resources.notes: Exercises and index are reserved for the paid print/ebook edition; the full instructional text is free.

resources.name: Data Carpentry: Foundations of Astronomical Data Science
resources.summary: Official Carpentries curriculum (2022) teaching ADQL/SQL database queries, Astropy/astroquery workflows and large-catalogue practices through a real science case (the GD-1 stellar stream in Gaia and Pan-STARRS data).
resources.access: Self-paced lesson free on the web; all data and notebooks downloadable; also taught at free community workshops.
resources.notes: Assumes basic Python and shell skills (Software Carpentry level).

resources.name: Astrobites
resources.summary: Daily plain-language summaries of new astro-ph papers written by graduate students since 2010, plus guides on applying to grad school, statistics and career paths; widely used to keep up with the literature.
resources.access: Web and RSS, no account; searchable archive by topic.

resources.name: Astronomy Stack Exchange
resources.summary: Question-and-answer site for astronomy with a substantial archive of answered questions, from observational practice to astrophysics calculations, answered by a mix of professionals and knowledgeable amateurs.
resources.access: Read without an account; free registration to ask or answer.
resources.notes: For software-specific questions, the astropy tag here and the OpenAstronomy forum overlap; research-level questions sometimes fare better on Physics Stack Exchange.

resources.name: OpenAstronomy Community Forum
resources.summary: Discourse forum where developers and users of Astropy, SunPy, lightkurve and related open-source astronomy packages answer usage and development questions; maintainers respond directly.
resources.access: Read without an account; free registration to post.

resources.name: Zooniverse
resources.summary: The largest citizen-science platform, born from Galaxy Zoo; hosts active astronomy projects (galaxy morphology, planet hunting, variable-star vetting) whose classifications feed published research, with talk boards connecting volunteers and science teams.
resources.access: Classify in the browser at zooniverse.org; free Project Builder lets researchers launch their own crowdsourcing project.
resources.notes: An account (free) is needed to save contribution history and to build projects; several projects list volunteer contributors on resulting papers.

resources.name: TIKE (Timeseries Integrated Knowledge Engine)
resources.summary: STScI's free JupyterLab platform running in the same AWS region as the MAST cloud archive, so TESS, Kepler/K2, Hubble and GALEX data can be analyzed at scale with no downloads; comes preloaded with lightkurve, astroquery and ~20 other packages.
resources.access: Log in at timeseries.science.stsci.edu with a free MyST account; no AWS account or payment details needed; tutorials in the TIKEBook (spacetelescope/project-tikebook on GitHub).
resources.notes: Modest per-user CPU/memory; meant for interactive analysis, not large batch production.

resources.name: SciServer
resources.summary: Johns Hopkins platform offering free Jupyter notebooks and persistent storage co-located with multi-terabyte datasets including the full SDSS catalogue databases (CasJobs), so survey-scale SQL plus Python analysis needs no local hardware.
resources.access: Free account at sciserver.org, then Compute (notebooks) and CasJobs (SQL with personal MyDB database).
resources.notes: Shared free resources with quotas; long-running jobs are queued. The standard companion to SDSS SkyServer for anything bigger than a browser query.

resources.name: NOIRLab Astro Data Lab
resources.summary: NSF NOIRLab's open science platform: tens of terabytes of survey catalogues (Legacy Surveys, NOIRLab Source Catalog, unWISE, Gaia and more) plus petabytes of images and spectra, with co-located Jupyter notebooks and TAP query services.
resources.access: Anonymous TAP/ADQL queries at datalab.noirlab.edu/tap (works from TOPCAT or `pip install astro-datalab`); free account unlocks the notebook server, personal database (MyDB) and virtual storage; example notebooks at github.com/astro-datalab/notebooks-latest.
resources.notes: Also hosts the SPARCL spectra service used for DESI and SDSS spectra.
